prompts.prompt:
Generate exactly ONE standalone 16:9 horizontal Chinese blog illustration, 1536x864 or another exact 16:9 canvas. Use case: illustration-story. Pure #FFFFFF white background, delicate slightly wobbly BLACK hand-drawn pen outlines, flat sparse color, abundant empty white space (at least 55%). No texture, shadows, gradients, gray wash, border, top-left heading, watermark, app UI, commercial vector illustration, PPT infographic or childish cute poster. Overall scene occupies central 60% width with comfortable margins. XiaoM must do the central conceptual action: a small serious deadpan mushroom creature with rounded RED cap, 3–5 WHITE polka dots, CREAM stem body, BLACK outline, tiny BLACK dot eyes, thin black arms and legs. Flat red cap and pale body, never solid black. Restrained BLUE annotations and thin ORANGE directional marks only. Black handwritten Chinese labels, sparse and legible. Do not add any text beyond the specified exact labels. One coherent metaphor, no panels, no collage.
Core idea: inspect the user's personal history BEFORE making a restaurant reservation. Physical scene: XiaoM is crouched over a large open accordion-fold personal-history notebook, actively lifting the most recent page with one hand and holding a magnifying glass over it with the other. On the most recent page, the only visible handwritten blue facts are “周日” and “6人”. A few older pages behind it are blank except tiny black pen lines, no other text. To the right, a simple unpressed reservation bell attached to a little blank reservation slip waits. A thin restrained orange curved arrow from the inspected newest page toward that bell implies next action, not already completed. Bell is a hand-drawn service bell, not a UI button. Exact Chinese labels only: “个人历史” beneath the open notebook; “周日” and “6人” on latest page; “再预订” beside the waiting bell. The magnifying glass and XiaoM's body connect the physical act of checking context. No top title. Keep action sparse, accurate and memorable: the actual plan is Sunday six people, no Saturday/five-person reservation is drawn.

Core idea: the total benchmark task pool is 265 entries, while 152 shared comparison tasks are a subset, NOT 265 tasks completed by every assistant. Invent a quiet physical metaphor: a wide shallow hand-drawn open archive drawer contains a few unnumbered white task cards, representing many, not literal counts. A removable narrow tray has just been partly pulled out from INSIDE that archive drawer by XiaoM, who is gripping its handle and carefully extracting it. The outer archive's small handwritten attached label reads exactly “总任务池 265”. The inner tray has a small BLUE handwritten label exactly “共同对比 152”. A thin orange short extraction motion mark only, not a flowchart arrow. The nested physical relationship must be unambiguous: tray belongs to the larger pool, the larger drawer still contains other cards, do NOT show two disjoint competing piles or sum the numbers. Main action is XiaoM selecting the common subset. Only those two text labels; no percentages, no leaderboard, no other numbers or text. Lots of white space. All task cards white with black pen outlines, no solid color boxes.

Core idea: turn an observed agent failure into a fixed repeatable regression test, not just patch it and forget. XiaoM is actively using a tiny hand-operated bookbinder, physically clipping a crumpled failure report into a clean ring-bound test notebook. The crumpled report on the left carries a small red X and exact Chinese label “失败记录”. The clean open test notebook on the right reads “回归用例”, with just two precise short handwritten checklist lines “同样输入” and “核对结果”. Tiny empty square checkboxes beside those lines, NO green success tick or fabricated passing result. XiaoM holds the report and works the binder lever, integrating failure evidence into a reusable test. A single thin ORANGE curling arrow around the notebook means rerun, not perpetual failure; sparse BLUE underlining only. Exact labels only: “失败记录”, “回归用例”, “同样输入”, “核对结果”. No code, no dashboard, no extra title, no performance claim. Bookbinder is a small absurd hand tool, sparse and clear, not an elaborate machine.
